summary: `logb`'s YAML defines `logb(x, b) => log_{b} (x)`: the value first, the base second. Four of its test cases read the base first: `logb(10::i64, 100000::i64) = 5.0`, `logb(2::fp64, 7::fp64) = 2.8073549220576041` (log₂ 7), `logb(7::fp64, 1.0::fp64) = 0` (log₇ 1) and `logb(2.34::fp64, inf::fp64) = inf`. By the YAML they are log₁₀₀₀₀₀ 10 = 0.2, log₇ 2 ≈ 0.356, log₁ 7 (a division by zero) and log_∞ 2.34 = 0. The cases further down the file (`logb(10::fp64, -inf::fp64)`, `logb(2.0::fp64, 0.0::fp64)`) also put the value second.
repro: [logb.test L5-L10](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/blob/b5aeda418813f657011bb82dd1300f996525c3ae/tests/cases/logarithmic/logb.test#L5-L10); [functions_logarithmic.yaml L152-L164](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/blob/b5aeda418813f657011bb82dd1300f996525c3ae/extensions/functions_logarithmic.yaml#L152-L164) names the arguments `x` and `base`, in that order.
handling: sverify reads `logb` as the YAML defines it. The four cases are triaged `case` in `upstream/substrait-cases.json`.
